interpretations: Average quantity per invoice is computed over Invoice_Line_Items.product_quantity (cast to number), the overall average is the mean of the per-invoice averages (each invoice weighted equally), and the cost ratio is (SUM(derived_product_cost) − SUM(derived_total_cost)) ÷ SUM(derived_total_cost).
The overall average is instead the mean of product_quantity across all line items (each line weighted equally), not the mean of per-invoice averages.
The "average of all the invoices' average quantities" is taken only over invoices that have a non-null average quantity (invoices with only null quantities are excluded from the overall average).
The cost ratio is the average of per-line (derived_product_cost − derived_total_cost) ÷ derived_total_cost, not the ratio of totals.
The cost ratio is (total derived_total_cost − total derived_product_cost) ÷ total derived_total_cost, with the opposite sign (the question's order is product_cost minus total_cost).
The cost ratio is divided by total derived_product_cost instead of total derived_total_cost.
Invoices whose total derived_total_cost is zero or null yield a null (or excluded) ratio and are kept in the list with a null ratio.
Invoices whose total derived_total_cost is zero or null are excluded from the results.
The cost-ratio totals ignore null values in each column separately (SUM skips nulls per column), so lines with only one of the two columns present still contribute.
The cost-ratio totals include only lines where both derived_product_cost and derived_total_cost are non-null.
The invoice list is limited to invoices appearing in Invoice_Line_Items (not all invoices in the Invoices table).
"Above" means strictly greater than the overall average; invoices equal to it are excluded.
"Above" means greater than or equal to the overall average; invoices equal to it are included.
The difference is the invoice's average quantity minus the overall average quantity (a positive number).
The difference is expressed as a percentage or ratio over the overall average rather than as an absolute difference.
Sorting is by the difference descending, with null differences placed last; ties are left in arbitrary order.
Sorting is by the difference descending, with ties broken by invoice number ascending.
The top 10 is the first 10 rows after sorting; if fewer than 10 invoices qualify, all of them are shown.
Output columns are: invoice number, average quantity, cost ratio, and difference, with unrounded full-precision values.
Because product_quantity is stored as VARCHAR, it is cast to a numeric type before averaging, and non-numeric strings are treated as null (ignored).
Because product_quantity is stored as VARCHAR, non-numeric strings are treated as 0 when averaging.
Integer division is avoided so that the averages and ratio are computed in floating-point or decimal arithmetic.
Integer division could apply to the averages, giving truncated results, if the quantity is cast to an integer.
queries:
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT invoice_number,
         AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty,
         (SUM(derived_product_cost) - SUM(derived_total_cost)) * 1.0 / SUM(derived_total_cost) AS cost_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
  GROUP BY invoice_number
)
SELECT invoice_number, cost_ratio
FROM inv
WHERE avg_qty > (SELECT AVG(avg_qty) FROM inv);
SELECT AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) FROM Invoice_Line_Items
SELECT AVG(avg_qty) FROM (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number) WHERE avg_qty IS NOT NULL;
SELECT AVG((derived_product_cost - derived_total_cost) / derived_total_cost) FROM Invoice_Line_Items
SELECT (SUM(derived_product_cost) - SUM(derived_total_cost)) * 1.0 / SUM(derived_total_cost) AS cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items
SELECT SUM(derived_total_cost) * 1.0 / SUM(derived_product_cost) AS cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items;
